root_causes.description: The frontend shows a severe latency regression: server-side p99 latency is pegged at 10000ms and user-facing spans (user_browse_product, user_get_recommendations) last ~15000ms. Frontend is also the only service in the cluster with a nonzero server error rate, consistent with client-facing slow responses/timeouts on the request path.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate max=0.019, mean=0.002 (only nonzero service in cluster; all others 0.000)

root_causes.description: Checkout spans carry the same ~15000ms durations as frontend (search p95_duration=46513ms) while its server error rate is 0.000, indicating checkout is blocked waiting on a slow downstream dependency (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, or product-catalog) rather than failing on its own.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 (no server errors; consistent with blocking, not failing)

root_causes.description: Recommendation sits on the slow request path (frontend → recommendation → product-catalog) and its user_get_recommendations call spanned ~15000ms, making it a candidate downstream source of the latency propagated to frontend and checkout.

remediation_steps: Isolate the slow downstream: compare per-service p99 latency for frontend's and checkout's downstreams (recommendation, product-catalog, cart, shipping, currency, payment, email) to find the single slow dependency.
Check frontend and downstream pods for CPU throttling / resource limits and verify request/upstream timeouts so slow calls do not pin requests at ~15s (frontend p99 pegged at 10s).
Roll back or restart the implicated downstream service if a latency fault or bad deploy is active in the 08:55–09:01 window.
Add alerting on frontend p99 latency and trace-duration SLOs to catch the regression before it surfaces as client-facing timeouts.
